abstract: Recursive algorithms are presented for computing the coefficients of a polynomial transformed by several commonly used transformations. The algorithms for performing the bilinear transformation and the geometric lowpass-to-bandpass transformation are particularly useful and can be readily implemented on small, programmable calculators and computers.

In extending some of the basic concepts of one dimensional system theory to two and multidimensional systems one encounters many difficulties. In this paper, discussion of such extension is reviewed and several counterexamples are given. In particular counterexamples to least square inverse polynomials, discrete Hilbert transform, bilinear transformation, necessary and sufficient conditions for linear time-invariant stability, primitive factorization for higher than two dimensional polynomial matrices and partial fraction expansion are given. Furthermore, several conjectures regarding the validity for such extensions are discussed.

It is shown that the ideal symmetrical twin-T built with zero tolerance components requires an ideal amplifier with infinite gain to sustain oscillations. A systematic procedure is outlined to find out the minimum amplifier gain required to sustain oscillations as well as the frequency at which the circuit will oscillate, knowing the nominal values and tolerances of each component of the passive twin-T.

articleTitle: A bibliography of Notch filters-active, passive, digital, lumped, distributed and integrated
abstract: A literature search on notch filters was performed and a bibliography of 160 references was compiled. The publications are listed chronologically in an alphabetical order for the last two decades to demonstrate the development of the state of the art of Notch filters.

articleTitle: Modeling of distributed lossless and lossy structures — A review
abstract: With the advances of the solid state art and the thin film technique, numerous structures and devices have been developed which essentially are distributed parameter ones. The passive distributed parameter structures possess extremely valuable properties. However, the tools available for analysis and synthesis of these structures are inadequate. A comprehensive review is presented of the modeling attempts made so far.

articleTitle: Optimal filter design using new formulas
abstract: Simple and fast method using new formulas is introduced to design a class of optimal RC ladder networks with double-terminations. These new formulas enable the designer to find optimal networks identical to those obtainable from existing techniques at a fraction of the time.

articleTitle: The case for a standard circuit format
abstract: Describes a standard circuit format which is a necessary prerequisite for making the use of a CAD system for system design economically attractive. This would allow a systems engineer to perform required tasks on an evolving design. The result would be a thorough and timely integrated system design.

The Science Research Council is part of the Department of Education and Science and is the largest government agency funding scientific research in universities, polytechnics and certain other establishments in the UK. Following a recent initiative by the SRC to boost engineering research and rationalize expenditure on the provision of computing facilities an interactive computing network (the ICF) is under intensive development. The author reports facilities and development of this interactive computing network.

The 1980 annual election is overshadowed by the U.S. general election, but each is important in its own way. I shall endeavor to explain why IEEE elections are important in more ways than one, and why your vote really does count.

It is argued that a `post VLSI technology' will employ some type of `continuum processor' (CP) and will require simultaneous development of a device technology and system design procedures for the technology.

Deals with optimal synthesis of an RC high-pass ladder network. It shows how to obtain a network with the maximum possible gain and minimum total series capacitance. The current transfer function, source and load conductances are specified. Lagrange multipliers method is used to obtain optimization. The entire process is completed using a microcomputer which can handle a large number of poles and can perform the optimization in a very short time.

ISCAS/80 was held in Houston, Texas on April 28–30, 1980; and over the months that have since gone by, it has been deeply gratifying to those of us involved in the organization of the meeting to receive from participants so many expressions of goodwill and appreciation.

articleTitle: Single-chip microcomputer application in high-altitude balloon orientation system
abstract: Describes the application of a single-chip microcomputer in a high-altitude balloon instrumentation system. The system, consisting of a magnetometer, a stepping motor, a microcomputer and a gray code shaft encoder, is used to provide an orientation reference to point a scientific instrument at an object in space. The single-chip microcomputer, Intel's 8748, consisting of a CPU, program memory, data memory and I/O ports, is used to control the orientation of the system.

articleTitle: Representation and simulation of digital filters
abstract: Straightforward conventions are described which allow an exact block diagram representation of digital filter structures. The description includes overload and quantization levels as well as the sequence of program execution. A digital filter simulation program is described which allows a choice of all register length and the type of arithmetic used. Each signal, each quantization perturbation and any functions of these are available for display. Application examples are presented.

articleTitle: Some pedagogical considerations of digital filter hardware implementation
abstract: Presents discussion pertaining to a read only memory (ROM) table look-up technique for implementing digital filters. This technique is very flexible in that a given digital filter can be implemented by merely changing the contents of the ROM. Sufficient detail is included so that the material can be used effectively for pedagogical purposes, as well as to ease the transition from design concepts to actual hardware implementation.

A literature search on distributed-RC networks was performed and a bibliography of 360 references was compiled. For easy access to the needed references, the bibliography is divided into 16 sections. A cross reference is given at the end of particular sections.

After returning from our annual conference (ISCAS), which was held recently in Houston, it is my pleasure to report to you that it was a great success. The program was well received. It gave an excellent insight into the many activities of our members and pointed out the trend in theory, education and applications of many areas in which our Society is involved in. The attendance reached a record "high" of about 750 people, many of whom came from Asia, Australia, Canada, Europe and the Middle East. The atmosphere was as usual informal, friendly and conducive to the exchange of ideas. I am sure that every one who attended the conference will join me in expressing our appreciation and thanks to Rui de Figueiredo, the General Chairman, and Ted Bickert, the Program Chairman, as well as to all of their committee members for their dedicated efforts to make this conference such a success.

Establishment by the USAB this year of Professional Activity Committees in (nominally) every IEEE Society provides us with a unique opportunity to debate the issues and express our concerns about our professional environment, from the perspective of the Society as a whole as well as our individual views. This PAC Report column has accordingly been initiated to appear regularly in the MAGAZINE, as a means of keeping you, the CAS Society membership, informed about IEEE professional activities and to encourage your interest and participation in PAC work.

As the year of 1980 phases out, I am addressing you for the last time in this column. A busy year passes fast, particularly when changes in technology and science dictate the pace. Our Society is no exception in finding a new orientation towards the future in technical as well as administrative activities. In both areas I can report some excellent progress which is the result of unrestricted support and cooperation by our officers and AdCom members as well as many experienced members of our Society.

This book is based on the author's lecture notes for sixth- and eight semester students of electrical engineering at the Universitat Karlsruhe in Germany from 1972–1976, a course given by the author at the University of Washington in 1975, and a summer course at the Centro de Investigacion del Instituto Politecnico National in Mexico City in 1976. Although there are several books on sensitivity, including textbooks in control and systems with chapters on sensitivity, this is the only textbook intended to be at the introductory level devoted exclusively to sensitivity theory. It is a welcome addition to the literature.

This book is intended for a first course in electronics for students at the junior level following a sophmore level course on linear circuit analysis. The author has been admirably successful in his stated goal of producing a book which discusses modern integrated circuit (IC) technology at the module level. A wide variety of circuit functions in IC form are described and their interaction with each other and the outside world is explained using only the stated prerequisite of linear circuit analysis. To achieve this, the author uses some unique and innovative approaches to modeling and has succeeded in generalizing the description of many circuit functions in a very lucid fashion.

articleTitle: Allen Gersho and B. Gopinath win Guillemen-Cauer award
abstract: This years' Guillemen-Cauer Award goes to Allen Gersho and B. Gopinath for their paper “Charge — Routing Networks ” published in the February 1979 issue of IEEE Transcribes on Circuits and Systems.

articleTitle: Gordon M. Jacobs, David J. Allstot, and Robert W. Brodersen win W.R.G. Baker prize award
abstract: This years' W.R.G. Baker Prize Award goes to Gordon M. Jacobs, David J. Allstot, and Robert W. Brodersen for their paper “Design Techniques for MOS Switched Capacitor Ladder Filters” published in the December 1978 issue of IEEE Transcribes on Circuits and Systems.

The Circuits and Systems Society has heard with regret of the death of Wolja Saraga on the 15th of February. His illness was comparatively short and during this time his wife, his relations and many friends were constantly with him. He continued working in this period and put the finishing touches to his two papers for the 1980ISCAS on the day before he died.

This text is intended for filter design and synthesis courses for junior/senior engineering students. As the author suggests quite correctly in the preface, this book is also suitable as an introductory exposition on electric filters to the practicing engineer with basic circuit theory background. Although the book is somewhat voluminous, it covers both analog and digital filter design fundamentals and would be a welcome addition in the general area of signal processing. In this context I would like to point out that most of the well-known texts on filters either talk about analog filters or digital filters only. Thus the reader of this book will be able to compare and contrast the merits and demerits of passive, active, and digital filters and design a proper filter best suited for his / her purpose. The treatment of materials in the book is quite thorough and rigourous. Numerous examples in the book help in the understanding of the theories developed. Problems included at the end of each chapter are straightforward and include some computer program development assignments. However utilization of the existing commercially available filter analysis and synthesis programs is not emphasized.

articleTitle: Wolja Saraga, David G. Haigh, and Robert G. Barker win Darlington Award
abstract: This years' Darlington Award goes to Wolja Saraga, David G. Haigh, and Robert G. Barker for their paper “Microelectronic Active-RC Channel Bandpass Filters in the Frequency Range 60–108 kHz for FDM SSB Telephone Systems” published in the December 1978 issue of IEEE Transcribes on Circuits and Systems.

This issue marks the beginning of the second year of publication for IEEE Circuits and Systems Magazine. As part of our continuing effort to improve the magazine, we begin in this issue a classified advertising column starting on p. 30. In addition, we have three excellent articles. The first, by Schmalzel, Hein, and Ahmed, presents a tutorial discussion of a ROM table look-up digital filter. The paper describes the dedicated-hardware digital filter in sufficient detail that one could easily implement the structure using off-the-shelf hardware. The second article, by Lim and Medley discusses microprocessor implementation of an optimization program for synthesis of RC high-pass ladder networks. Circuits with maximum gain and minimum total capacitance can be obtained using the program. The third article in this issue by Lim and Lee presents a high-speed algorithm for designing optimized doubly-terminated RC ladder networks.

As indicated by the title, the author has obviously set out to produce a research monograph addressing the model reference approach to adaptive control problems. Although control technology is a fairly broad field of interest, adaptive control is a very specialized part thereof, and the model reference approach is only one of several methods for addressing adaptive problems. Thus this book is intended for an unusually small audience.
